acceptanceCriteria: Record structured PASS/RETURN review verdicts and author resubmission with exact gate, candidate, attempt/generation and actor binding.
Expose current gate verdict/generation/resubmitted state to workState without parsing prose; stale verdicts and changed candidates invalidate as specified.
Independent regression tests cover reported false-PASS and misordered RETURN/resubmit cases; external verdict trust stays distinct from executable gate qualification.
Required contract, independent review, focused qualification, CEM/OCM, current-main integration and native completion/readback/audit are retained.
body:
Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/504; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Review verdicts (G1 matrix review, G2 lane review) exist only as markdown headings and bold lines in per-ticket status files, and the scheduler parses them. The parser misrouted tickets three times: prose "No G1 PASS is claimed" read as a pass; author sections titled "G1 RETURN repair dispositions" read as newer RETURNs, so a resubmitted matrix kept going to authors (10 of 24 sessions without progress); and a second RETURN that arrived after a resubmit line was invisible to the worker. Each cost many sessions before it was noticed.

## Request
Record verdicts as queue-native gate results (`gate record --ticket T --gate G1 --verdict PASS|RETURN --attempt A --reasons ...`), plus a `resubmit` event from the author, and expose them to `workState` (`gates: {G1: {verdict, generation, resubmitted}}`) so routing needs no text parsing. Related: #394 (acceptance verdict for new tests) would be a natural producer of the G2 record.

## Workaround in use
One parser module with regression tests built from the real misroutes.
